correctness.rationale: A complete self-contained proof in RESULT.md establishes a finite prime-local factorization and a CRT product of signed means; odd-prime means have odd-cardinality sign sums and never vanish. The binary recurrence is derived by even-term extraction; its opposite-parity dyadic numerator induction independently proves the unique zero family and unit-magnitude family. Conditioning on v2(n) relative to v2(c) yields the exact mixture (4), and solving its zero equation exhausts e=0,1,2 and excludes e>=3. The standard-library verifier independently checks 128834 integer/rational assertions, including direct product/LCM factorization over full small periods. Finitary checks are not relied upon for the infinite theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 finite-prime-power period theorem covers arbitrary multiplicative functions including the Liouville function, but period data does not determine zero versus nonzero average. The earlier exact value-frequency law covers each fixed progression b+a(n+i), including c-stride residue classes individually after splitting n modulo c; their finite weighted mixture can compute individual averages. It does not explicitly derive the uniform infinite two-parameter zero-set or the three v2(c) regimes. Its reduced-step prime-deletion law applies after fixing gcd(a,b), whereas the present n freely traverses both coprime and noncoprime classes. The combination supplies background tools, but the all-parameter zero-locus requires the binary-mean rigidity proof in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: A natural sign-invariant of arithmetic product/LCM windows receives an exact all-strides classification rather than a chosen parameter computation. Three disjoint 2-adic stride regimes reveal two genuinely new power-of-two balanced families and prove total disappearance of balance for strides divisible by eight. The distinction between sampling every initial integer and a fixed coprime progression is mathematically substantive. This is a motivated complete classification usable as a sharp benchmark for multiplicative-function LCM ratio distributions, without asserting downstream results.
